provenance: Stage-2 lane split applying the decision-agent's documented routing rule (detect-vs-hunt by detection feasibility, not severity: low=hunt, medium/high=detect) deterministically from each TTP's Stage-1 detection_feasibility assessment. Partition validated to cover the Stage-1 seed exactly with no overlap/dup; all ids verified present in the CI's bundled ATT&CK dataset.

detection_candidates.rationale: high — inbound mail with CHM/HTA attachments and business-proposal lures is detectable via mail-gateway attachment-type policy, sandbox detonation, and named-file (proposal_pakistan110.chm) indicators
medium — user opening a CHM/HTA spawning script interpreters is detectable via process-lineage (hh.exe/mshta.exe -> powershell.exe/cmd.exe) but depends on endpoint process telemetry

detection_candidates.technique_name: System Binary Proxy Execution: Compiled HTML File
detection_candidates.rationale: high — hh.exe executing a CHM from a user-download path and then spawning script interpreters is a rare, high-fidelity process-lineage detection
high — files carrying named alternate data streams (path:stream) and execution from an ADS are detectable via file-system telemetry (Sysmon FileCreateStreamHash EID 15) and ADS enumeration
high — script-block/module logging captures hidden -nop -w hidden downloadstring/IEX beacons and named .ps1 loaders; PowerShell spawned from hh.exe/mshta.exe adds high-fidelity context

detection_candidates.technique_name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Windows Command Shell
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — ncat.exe with the -e cmd.exe argument and cmd.exe children of unusual parents are detectable via command-line logging, but individual net/arp/whoami commands are common
high — PowerShell downloadstring and bitsadmin /transfer to raw IP:port URLs writing to CSIDL_APPDATA are detectable via process command-line, proxy and file-write telemetry
high — bitsadmin.exe /transfer with an external IP URL and the BITS-Client operational log (EID 3/4/59/60) provide high-fidelity detection of malicious BITS jobs

medium — high-volume, high-entropy DNS queries with long hex subdomains and repetitive AAAA responses to the same base domain are detectable via DNS analytics, but blend with legitimate DNS and require baselining — hunt-leaning
medium — HTTP beacons to raw-IP C2 on odd ports are detectable via proxy/netflow and JA3/beacon-interval analytics, but generic HTTP blends with normal traffic
medium — modified-base64 tokens in DNS labels/command lines are detectable via encoding/entropy heuristics, but require dedicated content inspection
medium — HTTP traffic on atypical ports (e.g. HTTP over 445/1003/1131) is detectable via protocol-vs-port mismatch analytics on netflow/proxy, but needs baselining

medium — plink/bitvise command lines with -proxytype/-proxyip and unexpected internal-to-external proxy chains are detectable via process command-line and netflow, but generic proxying blends with normal traffic

high — plink.exe (or renamed comms.exe) and Bitvise clients with port-forwarding (-R/-L) arguments, and outbound SSH from hosts that normally never initiate SSH, are detectable via process and network telemetry

medium — RDP (Type-10 4624) logons sourced from localhost/loopback tunnel endpoints or from hosts running plink/bitvise are detectable via correlation of logon and tunneling-process telemetry, but blend with admin RDP
high — process access to lsass.exe and Mimikatz signatures/command lines are highly observable via EDR process-access (Sysmon EID 10) and image-load telemetry
high — a dropped keylogger executable (Winit.exe) writing capture files and registering keyboard hooks is detectable via file-write, process and known-hash telemetry
medium — screenshot capture leaves limited discrete signal; detectable mainly via known backdoor behavior/hashes and image-file writes to staging paths — hunt-leaning
medium — recursive scans for web.config and reads of application config files are detectable via file-access telemetry and PowerShell script-block logs, but blend with legitimate admin/dev activity
medium — aspnet_regiis.exe invoked with -pdf/decrypt arguments outside a deployment context is an unusual, detectable command-line pattern, but is a legitimate admin tool

detection_candidates.technique_name: Create or Modify System Process: Windows Service
detection_candidates.rationale: high — new service installation (Event ID 7045 / 4697) with a name mimicking VMware but an unsigned/anomalous image path is a high-fidelity detection

detection_candidates.technique_name: Masquerading: Match Legitimate Resource Name or Location
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — vendor-like names in unusual paths and signed-tool binaries renamed (Plink -> comms.exe) are detectable via name/path/hash baselining and signature-vs-name mismatch

detection_candidates.technique_name: Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism: Bypass User Account Control
detection_candidates.rationale: high — the eventvwr.exe UAC bypass leaves a distinctive registry write (HKCU\Software\Classes\mscfile\shell\open\command) and eventvwr.exe -> mmc/powershell lineage, both high-fidelity detections
medium — net user and WMI account queries are detectable in command-line logs but are common admin actions; value comes from recon-burst/process-lineage correlation
medium — WMI queries (wmic/Get-WmiObject) are detectable via command-line and WMI-activity logging, but are common; suspicious mainly in a recon-burst context
medium — system-info enumeration is common and noisy; meaningful mainly within a tight recon-burst process-lineage window
medium — arp/ipconfig discovery commands are detectable via command-line logging but common; value comes from correlation within a recon burst
medium — netstat execution is detectable in command-line logs but common; meaningful within recon-burst context
medium — whoami is trivially detectable in command-line logs but extremely common; only meaningful in process-lineage/recon-burst context
medium — file/directory enumeration is common and noisy; meaningful mainly in a tight recon-burst process-lineage window

high — new script files written to web-server content roots, anomalous w3wp.exe/httpd child processes, and the specific webshell hashes are detectable via file-integrity monitoring and web-server process telemetry
medium — reuse of harvested valid credentials is detectable via anomalous-authentication analytics (new source host, first-seen credential, off-hours logon) but blends with legitimate use

detection_candidates.technique_name: Obfuscated Files or Information: Encrypted/Encoded File
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — high-entropy/encoded HTA and script payloads are detectable via file-entropy and encoding heuristics but require dedicated scanning

hunting_candidates.rationale: low — TLS-wrapped C2 content is opaque; detection relies on JA3/JA3S fingerprints, certificate anomalies and beacon-timing analytics rather than payload inspection — hunt-leaning
low — malware staging on adversary-controlled infrastructure occurs off-victim; intel/hunt candidate via infrastructure tracking and retro-hunting the staging IPs/URLs
